subject: PRS effect instead of SNP effects included in model?

messages.author: c06245755ba64e7c
messages.subject: PRS effect instead of SNP effects included in model?
parts:
Hello!

If conducting genomic SEM with two phenotypes/summary stats files, where, for phenotype 1, we have SNP effects, but with phenotype 2, we have no GWAS significant SNPs, would it be useful to instead use a PRS as an instrumental variable in the model? Second, we are not sure if it is feasible to feed in a PRS derived from the same summary statistics as used in the model for phenotype 2. This does seem problematic, but we were curious if others had thought this through at all? 


Thank you,

Christina

messages.author: 3b39745f73eec779
messages.subject: Re: PRS effect instead of SNP effects included in model?
parts:
Hi Christina,

you can (right now) use a few (say 1-50) SNPs in a GenomicSEM model as instrumental variables (in the same sense SNPs are used as instrumental variables in mendelian randomization). The reason a PRS (like  a PRS based on (almost) all SNPs) won't work is that all that information thats present in the summary statistics is already used in the model, its used to estimate the heritability, and the genetic covariance. So in effect you would be double counting them if you add a PRS.

If your PRS is a composite of a few SNPs that are not in LD you probably could add them to the model as a score, but I would favor adding them individually. In terms of what sumstats to use, the most important criteria is the following:

GenomicSEM work regardless of sample overlap between the GWASes, BUT using a SNP as instrument in genomicSEM you have to adhere to the laws of mendelian randomization, that is you can use the effect sizes in the GWAS IF the exposure and outcome GWAS do not have sample overlap, or if the exposure and outcome GWAS overlap you need to use an external GWAS to select which SNPS will serve as instruments.


Hope this helps,

Best,
Michel
